articles.title: United Airlines CEO faces rightwing backlash after calling for US wealth tax
articles.summary: Scott Kirby says wealth inequality is a ‘danger to society’ and calls for inheritance tax in recent interviewScott Kirby, the CEO of United Airlines, is under scrutiny from conservative politicians and commentators for saying wealth inequality is a “danger to society” and calling for a national wealth and inheritance tax in a recent interview.Talking to the New York Times, Kirby was asked about the growing public distrust of CEOs and whether he felt any responsibility to quell that distrust. Con...
articles.full_text:
Scott Kirby, the CEO of United Airlines, is under scrutiny from conservative politicians and commentators for saying wealth inequality is a “danger to society” and calling for a national wealth and inheritance tax in a recent interview.
Talking to the New York Times, Kirby was asked about the growing public distrust of CEOs and whether he felt any responsibility to quell that distrust.
“We should have a national wealth tax – it won’t work by state because people will just move,” he said. “And I think we should have inheritance taxes that get close to 100% at some level. I would pay them.”
In response, headlines from Fox Business and the New York Post decried that Kirby made $32m in 2025. In response to Kirby’s comments, Glenn Beck, a former Fox News host, and other users on X called for a boycott of United Airlines. Jeff Landry, Louisiana’s governor, said the statement was “audacious”.
“How audacious from a guy that didn’t even build @united and makes $32 million a year,” he wrote on X, adding a link to a government website to donate money to the government. “Better yet, he should distribute his salary to the employees at the bottom of the ladder @united!”
“Let’s see you step up and place your money where your mouth is!” Landry added.
The comment comes just two weeks before voters in California will decide on a so-called “billionaire’s tax”, which would put a 5% tax on the state’s billionaires, that the wealthy have been spending millions fighting against.
Kirby was also asked about the rising cost of flying and said that high prices this year were being compared to the “artificial low” prices from the pandemic, which largely halted travel and highly disrupted the airline industry.
“We have to charge enough that it covers the cost of flying, and it’s expensive to fly airplanes,” he said.
When asked about the $70 passengers must pay to sit in an aisle or window seat if they aren’t a frequent flyer with United, Kirby responded that “the way to give everyone what they want is to charge for the services and products that those customers want,” adding: “There are customers that pay more that get more.”
Kirby also maintained that fares were still lower than in 2019 after adjusting for inflation. According to data from the labor department, the index for airline fares increased by about 20% from September 2019 to September 2026, while overall consumer prices increased by 31%.

articles.title: US judge dismisses sexual abuse lawsuit from Sam Altman’s sister

Ann Altman accused the OpenAI CEO of repeatedly sexually abusing her more than two decades ago, which he has denied.In dismissing Ann Altman’s ⁠lawsuit, the US district judge Zachary Bluestone wrote that she had refused to appear for an independent medical examination despite warnings ⁠that failure to do ...
articles.full_text:
A judge dismissed a lawsuit filed by Sam Altman’s sister against him on Tuesday. Ann Altman accused the OpenAI CEO of repeatedly sexually abusing her more than two decades ago, which he has denied.
In dismissing Ann Altman’s lawsuit, the US district judge Zachary Bluestone wrote that she had refused to appear for an independent medical examination despite warnings that failure to do so would result in the case’s dismissal.
Laura Politi, a lawyer for Ann Altman, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Santos Perez, a lawyer who previously represented Ann Altman in the case but withdrew this month, said in a statement: “I am no longer authorized to comment on this case but I continue to believe in Annie.”
Ann Altman brought her lawsuit in St Louis, Missouri, federal court in January 2025.
Lawyers for Sam Altman did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Ann Altman accused her brother of sexually abusing and raping her between 1997 and 2006 at their family home in suburban Clayton, Missouri, starting when she was three and he was 12. She said the last acts of sexual abuse and rape occurred when Sam Altman was an adult. He is now 41.
The Altman family has said Ann Altman has mental health challenges and received financial support. Sam Altman has said she began accusing him on social media of sexual abuse after the family rejected her demands for more funds.

articles.title: European air fares could rise by as much as 20% in 2027, Ryanair boss predicts
articles.summary: Conflict in Middle East is pushing jet fuel costs higher and many carriers are not hedged against such increases, Michael O’Leary saysRyanair’s chief executive has predicted a record increase in European air fares next year, as airlines grapple with fuel bills pushed higher by the Middle East conflict.Many carriers are not hedged against rising jet fuel costs, Michael O’Leary said, which he predicted would lead to airline bankruptcies and takeovers. He forecast these pressures would result in th...
articles.full_text:
Ryanair’s chief executive has predicted a record increase in European air fares next year, as airlines grapple with fuel bills pushed higher by the Middle East conflict.
Many carriers are not hedged against rising jet fuel costs, Michael O’Leary said, which he predicted would lead to airline bankruptcies and takeovers. He forecast these pressures would result in the price of plane tickets rising by as much as 20%.
“You’re going to see air fares rise next year in Europe, I think by 10, 15, maybe 20%. You’re going to see the biggest increase in air fares, I would say, in history in Europe for the next 12 months,” O’Leary told a news conference in Brussels.
Jet fuel prices have soared in recent months, as the war on Iran has choked off fuel supplies. Jet fuel accounts for a large portion of carriers’ costs. The airlines body IATA previously predicted jet fuel prices would be 70% higher across 2026 – estimated to average $152 (£114) a barrel for the year, compared with $90 in 2025 – slashing airlines’ profits.
Ryanair and many other European airlines had hedged their jet fuel requirements for 2026, O’Leary said, adding that Ryanair was 80% hedged at $67 a barrel at the time the Iran conflict began in late February.
However, the boss of Europe’s largest airline said most European carriers, including Ryanair, do not have significant hedging in place from April 2027 onwards to protect them if oil prices remain high.
“We’re 85% unhedged next year, and most of the other European airlines are in a similar position,” O’Leary said.
Ryanair’s hedging contract for 2027 covered 15% of its fuel costs at $85 a barrel, he added, whereas spot rates are currently hovering at about double that level.
EasyJet reported a £105m annual rise in fuel costs in July, adding it had hedged 62% of its fuel requirements for the first half of 2027 and 37% for the second half of the year. The airline announced in October it was cutting 700,000 seats from its winter schedule in an attempt to save fuel.
During his visit to Brussels, O’Leary announced he was cutting 20 of Ryanair’s routes and more than one million seats from Belgium from the airline’s winter schedule, after the federal government’s decision to increase its aviation tax from €2 to €7 in January.
O’Leary is the latest executive to warn of the downbeat outlook for aviation. Industry leaders have said some carriers will struggle to survive the fuel price shock. Passenger surveys have shown travellers are braced for higher fares and are prepared to spend more, but airlines do not know how long consumers will be able to afford pricier tickets.

articles.title: Billionaire Mukesh Ambani launches India’s biggest-ever IPO
articles.summary: Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on WednesdayIndia’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday. C...
articles.full_text:
India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.
Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.
Set up a decade ago as a subsidiary of Ambani’s conglomerate Reliance Industries, and led by Akash Ambani, the oldest son of patriarch Mukesh, Jio offers low-cost broadband to millions of Indians.
Jio secured 212 anchor investors on Monday before its blockbuster IPO. They include some of the world’s largest fund managers, such as: BlackRock; Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund; the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority; Fidelity Investments; Schroders; JP Morgan Asset Management; Franklin Templeton; Invesco; and Prudential.
On Wednesday, shares will be offered to retail investors, and the IPO is set to close on Friday.
Reliance Industries said in a stock exchange filing last week that Jio had set a price range of 1,065 rupees to 1,119 rupees a share for its maiden share sale, offering up to 270m new shares.
The family-owned conglomerate has been encouraging its 400,000-plus employees to buy shares, offering them a discount of 54 rupees a share.
At the top end of the price range, Jio would be worth 10.3tn rupees, which would make it India’s fourth-largest company, behind its parent Reliance Industries, Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank. It would be more than twice as much as the 4.9tn-rupee valuation in 2020, when Meta and Google invested in the company.
However, the top valuation is far below initial expectations of more than £110bn when the telecoms group posted a draft prospectus in the summer.
It comes amid a broader stock market slowdown in India, with the blue chip Nifty 5o index down more than 12% this year.
Jio launched its telecoms services in September 2016. It gained 16 million subscribers in the first month, and topped 100 million subscribers within 170 days, according to Reliance Industries. It is credited with making mobile internet more affordable, by triggering a price war. The company intends to expand further into artificial intelligence, cloud computing and digital infrastructure.
Isha Ambani, who sits on Jio’s board as a director, told investors last week that the business idea was spawned by the poor connectivity she and her brother Akash faced when they returned to India on a break from studying in the US in about 2009-10. She struggled to submit a college assignment online because the internet was not working.
“What followed was a conversation about why should India be left behind,” she said. “Akash firmly believed that the answer and solution to this was creating a digital technology platform company.”
